relation.note: His master (ustādh) who promoted him to amir of ten, identified as Sultan al-Malik al-Ẓāhir Abū Saʿīd Jaqmaq on the basis of his nisbah 'al-Ẓāhir Jaqmaq'. Referenced by Wikidata QID (wd:Q647942) for uniformity of sultan references; the same person has an internal biographical entry in this corpus at AIND-D02423 (wd:Q647942 = #AIND-D02423).

event.desc: Promoted to amir of ten (imrat ʿashara) by his master, al-Ẓāhir Jaqmaq.
event.note: Occurred prior to holding the office of second dawādār.

event.desc: Appointed second dawādār by the son of his master (i.e. the son of al-Ẓāhir Jaqmaq), who is not named.
event.note: Occurred after being amir of ten and prior to his misfortune.

event.desc: Suffered misfortune, fled, and hid for several days.
event.note: Occurred prior to his arrest and relocation to Jerusalem.

event.desc: Arrested and ordered to relocate to Jerusalem as an unemployed person (baṭṭāl).
event.note: He remained in this status until his death in Shaʿbān 860 H.

person.note: アスンバーイ・アッ＝ザーヒル・ジャクマク、アル＝ジャマーリーおよびアッ＝サーキーとしても知られる。彼の師（アッ＝ザーヒル・ジャクマク）が彼をイムラ・アシャラ（十人長）に昇進させ、その後その師（ジャクマク）の息子が彼を第二ダワーダール（ドワーダール・サーニー）に任じた。しかし彼が失脚すると逃亡し、数日間身を隠した。その後拘束され、失業者（バッタール）としてエルサレムへ赴くよう命じられ、860年シャアバーン月に死去するまでその状態が続いた。

Asanbāy al-Ẓāhir Jaqmaq, also known as al-Jamālī and al-Sāqī. His master (al-Ẓāhir Jaqmaq) promoted him to amir of ten, and then his master's son appointed him second dawādār. When he suffered misfortune, he fled and hid for days. He was then arrested and ordered to proceed to Jerusalem as an unemployed person (baṭṭāl), a state in which he remained until his death in Shaʿbān of the year 860 H.
